scope: Where the frame time actually goes, and the largest available win

accounting_ms_per_frame_median.reading: the geometry construction is 44 per cent of a frame, more than motion and clustering together; the earlier profiles attributed this to the rail profile (about 18 ms, 854 median/mean calls per construction), rail-pair refinement (about 14 ms), normal covariances (7.3 ms) and the ground plane fit (4.3 ms)

opportunity_measured.idea: the ground and rail estimators do not need the walls, ceiling, ducts or the neighbouring track: rail returns lie at the gauge lines and the bed across the walkable width. Restricting their input to a lateral band should cost nothing in fitted geometry and much less in time.

straight_recording.band_2_0_m: 10420 points, 18.2 ms (55.6 ms full), anchor counts equal but rail anchors differ by up to 0.57 m - 2.0 m cuts into the neighbouring track's rail
straight_recording.band_2_5_m: rail anchors BIT-IDENTICAL (max |dx| 0.0000, max |dy| 0.0000), ground anchors and plane identical, rail head height identical

curved_recording.band_2_5_m_sensor_frame: 29516 points, 36.5 -> 29.0 ms, ground anchors and plane identical, but one rail anchor moves 0.0358 m laterally

opportunity_measured.conclusion: a lateral band around the CORRIDOR, not around the sensor axis, is the version to implement: on the straight recording it reproduces the geometry exactly, and the curved recording shows why the sensor-frame band is not enough - the corridor leaves the axis on a curve, so a sensor-frame band changes which rail returns are seen

not_shipped: no code change: the band as tested changes a rail anchor by 3.6 cm on the curve, which is decision-affecting, so it needs the corridor-aware form and the full gate (1460-frame panel identity, both recordings' statuses, labelled obstacle preserved) before it can be committed

also_measured.chain_filter_row_matching: np.unique over the cloud alone (72568 rows) is 21.9 ms, and the committed chain filter stacks every object's support on top of the cloud before that call - worth replacing with the object metadata it already carries (centre, extent, bbox), which gives the same cross-section position without the stack
also_measured.association: 10.1 ms for the assignment over roughly 200 tracks x 200 objects; the field's standard fix is a spatial gate that decomposes the assignment into small independent subproblems
